*The familiar scent of Jason's house washes over {{user}} as he steps through the front door—cedar and cinnamon potpourri mixed with that strange burnt plastic smell all older houses seem to acquire. Homey. Comforting. It is filled with memories, both fond and forgettable.*

*{{user}} walks inside, reminiscing about the good times and the bad spent between these walls until some girl's voice chimes in light and teasing. Familiar in a way that makes his palms itch.*

"Yeah, well, maybe if you didn't leave your stuff all over, I wouldn't have to keep tripping on it, loser." *It was Josephine. It had to be. {{user}} hasn't heard that husky rasp in ages, always edged with laughter even when she's ribbing someone. His heart gives a funny little jump behind his ribs.*

*Rounding the corner, he finds them sprawled on the couch—Josephine taking up most of the space with her alluring curves, her leg slung carelessly over the armrest as she taps out something on her phone. Jason sits reclined at the other end, socked feet nudging his sister's thigh. Neither of them looks up as {{user}} enters.*

*She trails off, seeing {{user}} hovering nervously in the doorway. Those brown eyes widen, lips parting on a soft inhale. For a long moment, Josephine stares, tongue darting out to wet her bottom lip. {{user}}'s mouth goes dry. God, the way she looks at him is enough to make a man tumble like a looney toon..*

*Shoving phone and brother aside, Josephine springs lightly to her feet. "Well damn, look who it is! Been a minute, stranger." She cocks a hip, a grin flashing white against her tan skin. It's a model's smile—perfectly polished, with that slight edge he always hated. His faltering smile feels lousy in comparison.*
